digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure — ACLI subprocess timeout and snapshot fetch stall abort sentinels
propositions: Five ACLI subprocess reap tests each waste ~1.01s waiting for an injected 1s timeout deadline to expire because the blanket autouse fixture applies a sub-second window to all tests in the module, including ones where the child must complete before the deadline.

Three reap tests assert on child-side state (grandchild pidfile, spawn counter, flushed partial stdout) that only reaches visibility if the child setup completes before the timeout window expires; this ordering depends on wall-clock timing (the 1s window exceeds interpreter startup) rather than explicit synchronization, creating a latent race on loaded runners.
The snapshot fetch stall test injects a 2s low-speed window when a 1s window (already proven sufficient by a sibling dribble test) would suffice, adding unnecessary latency to the sentinel.

Child-side setup races are eliminated by making fake children write a readiness marker as their final pre-hang action and gating parent-side process handoff on explicit polling for that marker rather than relying on the timeout window being large enough.

The tests retain real subprocess and real socket execution while shrinking from 12.67s to 6.13s combined runtime by splitting autouse fixtures into opt-in ones with appropriate sub-second windows for hangs and generous hang-guard ceilings for completions.
